summary: Ran step M1-S05 of build tier2-webhook. build_plan.py next listed it as the only runnable step; it was claimed running, its owning agent metadata-builder was executed inline per the invocation instruction, and it returned a built envelope with no refusal. check-outputs exited 0 on both declared outputs, so the step was set built. The owning agent wrote artefacts/M1-S05/package.xml (7 types blocks, 33 members, version 67.0, no wildcards) and artefacts/M1-S05/deploy-order.md. Nothing was written outside artefacts/M1-S05 and envelopes/M1-S05; no relocation was needed because metadata-builder is build-aware. Two plan-text defects were carried into the envelope rather than worked around: inputs.members.ApexClass names 11 classes where the artefacts carry 13, and inputs.deploy_order sequences the PermissionSet ahead of the fields it grants.
confidence_rationale: Step 9 rubric: the step was in next, every required input of the owning agent resolved from the plan, both envelopes validate, check-outputs exited 0 and nothing landed outside artefacts/M1-S05 - which is the HIGH row - except that two of the step's bound inputs contradicted the artefacts they describe, so the owning agent had to resolve membership and ordering against the upstream outputs. That is not a HIGH-row 'resolved from the plan'.

process_observations.observation: The owning agent is build-aware - grep for artefact/build_dir/step_id/.sfskills over its AGENT.md returned 39 - so it wrote straight onto the declared output paths and no Step 7 relocation was needed.

The step carried human_gate false and its four dependencies were all documented, so build_plan.py next listed it without any of the three Step 2 blockers, and set-status running was accepted first time.

Two of this step's bound inputs describe the build as it stood before the M1-S03 and M1-S04 rebuilds: inputs.members.ApexClass enumerates 11 classes where 13 exist, and inputs.deploy_order sequences PermissionSet ahead of the object and field metadata its fieldPermissions rows name.

Step 5 of this agent's own playbook makes step inputs the winning source and forbids an invocation from correcting them, while the step's declared manifest acceptance test requires every artefact file to be covered by a member; the two point opposite ways here, and the artefacts were followed because the acceptance test is what gates the step and the input's own prose is a description of the members rather than a constraint on them.

Neither agent's Wave 10 report pair under docs/reports/ was written, because this invocation constrained all writes to the build directory; the build-scoped envelope pairs are the only record of both runs.
M1-S05 is the last step of M1; every other step is documented, so the milestone is one tester and one doc-keeper pass from the G3 gate.
process_observations.followup_reason: M1-S05's four acceptance tests - the declared checker, the xml parse, the build-wide manifest consistency check and the manual deploy-order read - are the tester's to run.
